title: Covering Relation and the Hasse Diagram
quickIdea: The Hasse diagram drops the self-loops and every arrow that transitivity can rebuild. What is left is the covering relation, and it is a complete picture of the poset.
remember: b covers a when a < b and no element lies strictly between them. The Hasse diagram draws one upward segment for each covering pair.
Edges of the Hasse diagram = covering pairs. The full relation is the reflexive transitive closure of those edges, so no information is lost.
To read the diagram: a <= b exactly when some upward path runs from a to b. Unrelated elements simply have no path in either direction.
A diagram is a Hasse diagram only if it is drawn so that a covering pair is one segment with no element in between - a diagram that hides a covering pair behind a vertex is unreadable, not wrong.
For divisibility on {2, 3, 6, 12, 24} the covering pairs are (2,6), (3,6), (6,12), (12,24): four edges, while the relation itself has 14 pairs.
For divisibility on the eight divisors {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24} there are 10 covering pairs.
The number of edges is not the number of pairs: |R| - |A| counts the non-reflexive pairs, and the diagram usually shows far fewer.

example.prompt: X = {2, 3, 6, 12, 24} ordered by divisibility. Draw the Hasse diagram, count its edges, and count the pairs of the relation.
example.work: 2 and 3 are incomparable, both divide 6, 6 divides 12, 12 divides 24. Covering pairs: (2,6), (3,6), (6,12), (12,24) - four edges. The full relation: 2 relates to 2, 6, 12, 24 (4 pairs); 3 relates to 3, 6, 12, 24 (4); 6 to 6, 12, 24 (3); 12 to 12, 24 (2); 24 to 24 (1).
example.answer: 4 edges in the Hasse diagram and 14 ordered pairs in the relation.

gateAngle: GATE CSE 1996 asked for exactly this edge count on this set. The two-step method - find covering pairs, then count by multiples - answers both the edge question and its common variation, the cardinality of the relation.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: GATE CSE 1996: X = {2, 3, 6, 12, 24} with x <= y when x divides y. The number of edges in the Hasse diagram is 3, 4, 9, or none of these.
variations.why: Only the four covering pairs are drawn; the transitive pairs 2-12, 2-24, 3-12, 3-24 and 6-24 are recoverable from the paths and are not edges.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: For the same poset, what is the cardinality of the relation, and how many of its pairs are not shown as edges?
variations.answer: 14 pairs in the relation; 10 of them are not edges.
variations.why: 14 pairs minus the 4 edges. The 10 are the 5 reflexive pairs plus the 5 transitive shortcuts - the count GATE asks when it varies the question.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: A Hasse diagram has 7 vertices and 8 edges and is drawn with no self-loops. What is the smallest possible cardinality of the underlying relation?
variations.answer: At least 15 pairs, because the 7 reflexive pairs are always in the relation.
variations.why: The diagram shows only the 8 covering pairs; the relation must also contain all 7 reflexive pairs and every transitive shortcut, so 15 is a floor, not the answer in general.

trap.what: Counting the edges of the Hasse diagram as if they were the relation, or drawing a transitive edge.
trap.why: The diagram is the covering relation: transitivity is applied by the reader, not drawn. Reading a diagram, students also forget that a path of length two already means a <= b.
trap.counterexample: In the 4-element chain a < b < c < d the relation has 10 pairs but the diagram has only 3 edges; drawing the pair (a, c) as an edge would be a drawing error, not a different poset.

check.question: In the Hasse diagram of the divisors of 12 ordered by divisibility, how many edges are there?
check.explanation: The divisors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Covering pairs: 1-2, 1-3, 2-4, 2-6, 3-6, 4-12, 6-12. That is 7. The pair 2-12 is not an edge because 2 < 6 < 12.
